context.body: Selected for the reader trail because “The servant rejected, wounded, silent, and allotted a portion” preserves a distinct antecedent source unit within anticipation.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: A communal “we,” the servant, the LORD, oppressors, and later offspring appear without collapsing into one voice.
observations.label: The servant rejected, wounded, silent, and allotted a portion: textual observation

observations.body: Rejection and wounds lead through silence, judgment, grave, offering, sight, knowledge, bearing, and allotted portion.
observations.label: The servant rejected, wounded, silent, and allotted a portion: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: Bearing language recurs around griefs, sicknesses, iniquities, and sins.
observations.label: Relationships named in Isaiah 53:1–12

payload.posture: Read Isaiah 53:1–12 as its own anticipation and stated approach crucifixion setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The servant is acted upon and also described as acting, while the passage attributes outcomes to the LORD.
payload.title: The servant rejected, wounded, silent, and allotted a portion
